---
title: "Lab 0 — Getting Set Up"
subtitle: "Ungraded, but required · due before class Sep 24"
---

**Due: before class on Thursday, September 24** (Lab 1 happens in class that day and assumes all of this works).
**Time needed: ~30–45 minutes.** Do it this week — if anything fails, come to office hours or email the TAs *before* Sep 24, not the night before.

By the end of this lab you will have: (1) a working JupyterHub login, (2) a GitHub account with a private course repository shared with the teaching staff, and (3) one completed notebook pushed to that repository and linked on Courseworks. This is the exact workflow you'll use to submit every lab and homework this semester.

---

## Part A — Accounts (10 min)

1. **GitHub.** If you don't have an account, create one at [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup). Use a professional-ish username (it may end up on your CV — many of you will link to course projects later). Enable two-factor authentication (GitHub requires it).
2. **JupyterHub.** You will receive an invitation to the course computing hub at **[HUB-URL — to be announced on Courseworks]**. Log in with the credentials from the invite and confirm your server starts (click "Start My Server" and wait for the JupyterLab interface to load).

> **If the hub won't start for you:** email the TAs with a screenshot. As a backup, every course notebook also runs on [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com) — but sort out your hub access this week regardless; we'll need it for the second half of the course.

## Part B — Run the verification notebook (10 min)

1. Download `verify_setup.ipynb` from the Courseworks Lab 0 assignment page.
2. On the hub: drag-and-drop the file into the JupyterLab file browser (left panel).
3. Open it and run every cell (`Shift+Enter`, or Run ▸ Run All Cells).
4. Fill in your name/UNI where indicated and make sure the final plot appears with no errors.

## Part C — Create your course repository (15 min)

1. On GitHub, click **New repository**:
   - Name: `climate-modeling-f26-<your-uni>` (e.g., `climate-modeling-f26-ab1234`)
   - Visibility: **Private** ← important
   - Check "Add a README file"
2. Add the teaching staff as collaborators: repo **Settings → Collaborators → Add people** — add **`[INSTRUCTOR-GITHUB]`**, **`[PRANI-GITHUB]`**, and **`[CHANDANIE-GITHUB]`**.
3. Put your completed notebook in the repo. Two ways — pick one:
   - **Easy way (fine for today):** on your repo's GitHub page, **Add file → Upload files**, drag in the completed `verify_setup.ipynb` (download it from the hub first: right-click the file → Download), and click *Commit changes*.
   - **Real way (we'll all use this from Lab 1 on):** in a hub Terminal (File → New → Terminal):
     ```bash
     git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/climate-modeling-f26-<uni>.git
     cp verify_setup.ipynb climate-modeling-f26-<uni>/
     cd climate-modeling-f26-<uni>
     git add verify_setup.ipynb
     git commit -m "Lab 0: verification notebook"
     git push
     ```
     GitHub will ask you to authenticate — you'll need a **personal access token** instead of your password: GitHub **Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Tokens (classic) → Generate new token** (scope: `repo`; set expiration to end of December). Paste the token when `git push` asks for a password. Save it somewhere — you'll reuse it all semester.

## Part D — Tell us it's done (2 min)

On Courseworks, open the **Lab 0** assignment and submit **the URL of your repository** (e.g., `https://github.com/ab1234/climate-modeling-f26-ab1234`). That link-posting step is how every submission works this term: work lives in your repo, the Courseworks link + timestamp is what makes it official.

---

### Checklist
- [ ] Hub login works, server starts
- [ ] `verify_setup.ipynb` runs top to bottom with your name and a plot
- [ ] Private repo `climate-modeling-f26-<uni>` exists, staff added as collaborators
- [ ] Notebook is in the repo
- [ ] Repo URL posted to Courseworks Lab 0
